svg.text: Width builds bumps one at a time; depth doubles the teeth at every layer
one hidden layer: four ReLUs make one bump
Add one bump per region you want to fit. In d dimensions that is
about (1/epsilon)^d bumps - the curse of dimensionality.
depth: composing one triangle map with itself
1 layer: 2 pieces 2 layers: 4 3 layers: 8 k layers: 2^k
A single hidden layer needs at least 2^k - 1 units to match.
At k = 10 that is 30 units with depth against 1,023 without; at k = 20, 60 units against roughly a million.
This is a proved separation, not a heuristic: some functions are cheap for deep nets and provably expensive for shallow ones.
What the universal approximation theorem promises is that the shallow net CAN do it.
What it never promises is that the cost is reasonable, or that training will find the weights.
